notes: Known-answer navigation tasks for the javascript lane. Needle-based, not line-based: bench/verify-tasks/verify.mjs resolves every needle to a unique line at the current SHA, so the manifest survives edits without stale line numbers. Paths are relative to the lane root (javascript/), not to the repository root. 'expect' blocks carry the ground truth a harness scores against. A count is a minimum only where its field name starts with min_ (min_symbols, min_incoming); every other count is exact. On an implementation or cardinality task, exact_count counts concrete, non-generic, unconditionally computed impls only. On an implementation or cardinality list, optional_sites names declarations that satisfy the contract but are not counted; a tool may return them or not. A declaration is listed there when it is a base class under packages/bench/src/support/ that satisfies the contract by shape but whose contract member, resolved along its prototype chain, is a stub whose body only throws, so the class is abstract and never the concrete answer: AbstractNotifier (send), AbstractExporter (export), AbstractReport (rows), and AbstractPeriodicReport and AbstractCompositeReport, which inherit AbstractReport's rows unchanged. Each base was read against that criterion; the lists rest on the source, not on any tool's output. cfg-gated impls are excluded. On the implementation surface exact_count counts concrete classes only: JavaScript has no implements keyword, so satisfaction is structural and reached through the prototype chain, and the abstract bases (AbstractReport, AbstractPeriodicReport, AbstractCompositeReport, AbstractNotifier, AbstractExporter) are excluded from every count. Counting rules for the other count-bearing fields, each stated the way the current counts were made. references: a site is one line, so a line that names the symbol twice is one site. The lines searched are the .js, .cjs and .mjs files under packages/*/src and packages/*/tests; README prose, bench/ and the deliberately unparseable fixtures/broken-syntax files are outside the count. A line counts when the symbol appears on it as code (a call, member read, construction, argument, operand or assignment target), as a binding (an import or export specifier, a destructuring of require(...), a module.exports shorthand entry, a name a JSDoc @import tag binds) or as a JSDoc type reference (an @param, @returns, @type, @property or @typedef type, including import("...").X and a local @typedef alias of the same name). It does not count when the symbol appears only in comment prose, only inside a string literal, or only as a property key of a JSDoc type literal ({ X: ... }), and the task's from line, which holds the declaration, is never counted. Each counted symbol has exactly one declaration in the lane, and every method call was checked to have a receiver of the declaring class, so every counted line refers to that declaration. exact_count on a references task is the number of counted lines: the known_sites entries plus the lines of every repeated_sites entry. repeated_sites names a needle written identically on several lines of one file; lines is the number of lines it matches, and each of those lines is one site. optional_sites on a references task names lines a tool may return or omit, outside exact_count: a JSDoc type-literal key, and for name_only the lines that carry the constant holding the string instead of the string itself. On a name_only task the counted lines are the code lines that write the literal string, the from line excluded. card-rule-contract: nominal_count counts the implementors declared as classes (one class per file under rules/, reaching the contract's members through its prototype), structural_count counts the plain object literals in rules/structural.cjs that carry the contract's members, and exact_count is their sum. multi-parent: extends_count counts the class's extends parent (one), implements_count counts the mixin objects Object.assign copies onto its prototype, and exact_count, where given, is their sum. call_hierarchy: min_incoming is a floor on the number of distinct callers, a caller being the innermost function, method or test callback that encloses a call line (the call lines themselves are not the unit); incoming_includes names one call line per caller. candidate names the declaration the answer must land on (resolution, direction and import-precision tasks). A resolution task that also states exact_count has a call that can dispatch to more than one declaration at run time: exact_count counts them, known_sites lists them all, and candidate is the one the default binding reaches. known_sites outside references: on a definition, resolution or import-precision task that states exact_count, known_sites lists exactly the counted answers; on any other task it names context lines the answer passes through or rests on and carries no count, namely a re-export hop, the import that brings in a built-in parent, a createRequire binding or a @template tag on a definition task, and on card-rule-contract the registry lines that collect the implementors, whose exact_count is taken over implementations. must_not_include lists what a correct answer never contains, each entry written in the task's own terms (a declaration name, a file path, a kind name, a phrase or a code fragment): the near miss a careless resolver would report instead of the target, such as a namesake declaration or the file that holds it, the wrong end or direction of a parent edge, a re-export or barrel file the answer passes through, a sibling name the import does not bind or read, a runtime require a type-only import never creates, and on a lane_local task a sibling lane's directory prefix. Kinds added by the fifth wave: builtin_parent (extends a node built-in), same_name (two exports with one name in different modules), jsdoc_generic (a JSDoc @template type parameter, which exists only in the comment and has no runtime form), dynamic_import (import() with a static specifier). Kind added by the implementation surface: structural (the implementor never names the contract, which is a JSDoc @typedef with no runtime declaration), glob (`export *`, whose exact_count is the number of names crossing the re-export), namespace_import (`import * as`, where the answer is the one member actually read off the namespace object). IDs shared with the php, rust, typescript, python and go lanes ask the same question in each language. document_symbol tasks count the named symbols the anchored FILE declares: every module-scope class, function and variable (constant) declaration, exported or not, and every member written in a class body (constructor, methods, accessors, static members and fields). Not counted: import bindings and require bindings (const X = require(...) and const { X } = require(...)), anything declared inside a function, method or static-block body (locals and parameters), members created by assignment (this.x = ... in a constructor, X.prototype.y = ...), object-literal keys, module.exports entries, and JSDoc @typedef or @callback names, which are documentation, not declarations. Each task's note enumerates that count N and states min_symbols = floor(0.75 * N), the 25% margin absorbing listings that fold container nodes. call_hierarchy tasks name callees under outgoing_includes and callers under incoming_includes; both are file+needle pairs the verifier resolves. Route tasks (def-route-to-handler and the def-route-<framework> ids shared with the typescript lane) ask which handler serves a named route, keyed file+needle like any definition, the answer being the handler declaration in the framework's own shape and never packages/routes/src/reportPayload.js, the body every packages/routes handler shares. Where routes are registered in code (express, hono, fastify) the from line is the registration call and from.symbol the handler. Where nothing in code names the handler (nestjs, whose decorators plain JavaScript applies as calls that name the method by string, and the file-convention frameworks remix, sveltekit, nuxt and expo, whose route is the module's file path) the task is a string-keyed link: the from line is a committed consumer that addresses the route by its URL (a redirect, a fetch, a request-level test), from.symbol is the path token of that URL string, and the framework's convention, not any identifier, binds the path to the handler. Other kinds this lane uses: string_key (on a definition task: the module a call reaches is chosen at run time by a string, a specifier read out of a frozen map and passed to a createRequire require; the answer is every declaration that string can select, listed under known_sites and counted by exact_count, the line asked from is not one of them, and must_not_include names the files of the contract's other implementors, which no key selects), barrel (packages/core/src/index.js declares no name of its own and only forwards exports, so an import from @atelier/core resolves through it to the declaring module and never stops on the index file), mixin_parents (a class whose parents are one extends edge plus mixins copied onto its prototype with Object.assign: only the extends parent is visible at the class line, yet every one of them counts as a parent, either as exact_count or as extends_count plus implements_count), name_only (the subscribe call writes the event name "repair.completed" as a bare literal and no symbol reference links it to the emit path; the dispatch side may pass the REPAIR_COMPLETED constant, but only the matching string value ties the two together), shadow_alias (a rename of one of two same-name export class Formatter declarations, written as an ESM import { Formatter as X }, a CommonJS destructuring rename { Formatter: X } = require(...), a JSDoc type written against such an alias, or a JSDoc @import { Formatter as X } tag, which renames for types only and creates no runtime binding: it resolves to the class in the module the import names, never its namesake), syntax_error (a negative-case fixture with an unclosed class body, an unbalanced destructuring pattern, or TypeScript-only syntax, type annotations and an interface declaration, in a .js file: any JavaScript parser has to fail on it rather than invent closing braces, strip the types and resolve halfway), type_only (a JSDoc type reference such as @type {import("...").X}, which creates no runtime edge: the file never requires the module it names). Kinds shared with other lanes, worded identically in every lane that uses them. child_of: the anchored declaration is the child end of a parent edge, and the answer is a direct parent it extends, implements or embeds, one level up, never a further ancestor and never one of its own children. imports: an import that binds only the names it lists; the answer is each named declaration in the file that declares it, never a sibling declared beside it and never every name the target module exports. lane_local: a symbol every lane carries under the same name or as its lane equivalent (Money, Customer, Dataset, the reference prefix, the invoice calculator's calculate, the billing Formatter); resolution must land on this lane's own declaration and never cross into a sibling lane. parent_of: a parent edge scored for direction, with the anchor at either end; the parent is the type that is extended, implemented or embedded, the child is the type that does so, and an answer that reports the child as the parent is wrong. unresolvable_static: an import whose target module is built from a runtime value, so no single module is the static answer; the honest result is every candidate module, and exact_count counts them. uses_self: a type that refers to itself, such as a tree node holding children of its own type; the edge is a uses edge back to the declaring type, never extends, implements or embedding. List fields. symbols (document_symbol) is the complete list of the names counted under the document_symbol rule above, so its length is N, and min_symbols is floor(0.75 * N); must_include (document_symbol) is the subset of symbols a correct listing must contain, each entry a name from symbols; on a parse-negative task must_include is instead a substring the reported diagnostic must contain (the fixture name token). implementations (implementation, cardinality and multi-parent tasks) holds one file+needle entry per counted declaration, so its length equals exact_count where one is stated (and extends_count + implements_count on parents-class-one-plus-two); optional_sites declarations are never in it. from.symbol is the identifier a task asks about, exactly as written on the from line and with no qualifier: the alias where an alias is used, the member on a member access, null when the question has no single identifier. from.occurrence (1-based) says which one when it appears more than once on that line, and is then required. document_symbol, parse-negative and diagnostics tasks ask about a file and carry neither key.
